title: Room Entities, DAOs, Relationships, and Transactions

scout.purpose: Room gives compile-time SQL verification and coroutine/Flow integration, while schema, keys, relationships, and transaction boundaries remain application design decisions.
scout.realWorldUse: Articles, authors, bookmarks, remote keys, queued mutations, and cache metadata require durable relational invariants and observable queries.
scout.outcome: Design normalised entities and indices, expose focused DAOs, query relationships, and keep multi-step invariants inside database transactions.

blocks.text: An Entity maps to a SQLite table with a stable primary key, columns, indices, and optional foreign keys. Database entities are persistence models, not network DTOs or domain UI models. Choose keys from durable identity rather than list position. Add indices for measured query and relationship needs, understanding write and storage cost. Foreign-key actions define what happens on parent update or deletion; Room does not allow object references between entities because database relationships are queried explicitly.

blocks.caption: A stable primary key, measured index, observable query, and upsert form a focused persistence boundary.

sections.title: DAOs expose queries rather than tables

blocks.text: A DAO groups focused SQL operations and Room validates queries against the schema. suspend fits one-shot insert, update, delete, or result; Flow observes query tables and re-emits after relevant invalidation. Returning an entity list exposes persistence schema, so repositories often map DAO models to domain. Relationships can use explicit joins, multimap results, or intermediate data classes with Embedded and Relation. Avoid N+1 repository loops when one SQL query can express the relationship.

blocks.caption: A stable primary key, measured index, observable query, and upsert form a focused persistence boundary.

blocks.title: Room validates SQL, not product meaning
blocks.text: Keys, conflict rules, transaction scope, and domain mapping still require design.

withTransaction or a Transaction DAO method makes a set of statements atomic. Use it when replacing a page with remote keys, applying a queued mutation and marking it complete, or reading a consistent multi-query relationship. Keep network calls outside the database transaction because long external waits hold resources and cannot roll back the server. Concurrent writers still require conflict strategy and unique constraints. Test rollback after an injected failure and verify flows publish only committed state.

Production data work must remain correct after interruption and repetition. Define the source of truth, stable operation identity, transaction boundary, cancellation behaviour, and the state shown before remote confirmation. Exercise empty and stale data, malformed input, duplicate delivery, simultaneous callers, process death, schema upgrade, storage pressure, and connectivity restoration where relevant. Use pure unit tests for mapping and conflict policy, real Room or DataStore instances for persistence contracts, MockWebServer for protocol behaviour, and WorkManager test APIs for durable scheduling. Logs must reveal operation state without exposing tokens, user content, or personal identifiers. A future engineer should be able to explain which component owns every row, cursor, credential, retry, and final user-visible outcome.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name authority, identity, lifetime, failure, cancellation, and recovery.

steps.label: Persist intent
steps.detail: Commit user-visible state or queued work before unreliable boundaries.

steps.label: Execute
steps.detail: Perform the smallest idempotent or transactional operation.

steps.label: Reconcile
steps.detail: Merge authoritative outcome and resolve conflicts deliberately.

steps.label: Verify
steps.detail: Test interruption, recreation, migration, duplication, and offline recovery.

blocks.title: Never hold a database transaction across network I/O
blocks.text: The remote call cannot participate in SQLite rollback and prolongs locks.

inspect.title: Move the network call outside transaction
walkthrough: The transaction remains open during an unpredictable remote operation.
SQLite resources and concurrent access are held while no local invariant changes.
Fetch first, then transactionally replace related local rows and keys.
inspect.expectedOutput: Network delay holds no database transaction and local page replacement is still atomic.

trap_check.mistake: Using one Article class for DTO, Entity, domain, and UI.
trap_check.why: Wire and schema evolution become coupled to every layer.
trap_check.fix: Map explicit persistence entities at the repository boundary.

trap_check.mistake: Adding a retry, cache, or abstraction without naming the failure contract.
trap_check.why: The implementation hides ambiguity while duplicate, stale, or lost outcomes remain possible.
trap_check.fix: Write the invariant and an interruption test before introducing machinery.

challenge_intro.task: Design article, author, bookmark, remote-key, and pending-mutation entities with DAOs, indices, relationships, atomic page replacement, and rollback tests.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Stable keys and uniqueness protect identity. No network call runs inside a transaction. Relationship and rollback behaviour is tested on Room.

recall.answer: A durable table schema and constraints.
All enclosed local statements commit or roll back together.
